contract.intent: Create self-verifying immutable recovery evidence outside the primary database so one completed cycle can be restored into entirely new relational and object targets without mutating old targets.
contract.truth_owner: Backup bytes plus canonical self-digested checkpoint/object manifests and a restore receipt own recovery evidence; the primary operational database cannot be the sole owner of its own backup receipt.
contract.cycle_boundary: One checkpoint binds exactly one completed scheduled-cycle identity/digest/slot and the database/object state represented by its backup. Stale, nonterminal or ambiguous cycles fail.
contract.database_boundary: Inventory and verification operate on the backup/restored target, not an independently racing live query; every table count and canonical rowset digest, schema revision and strict integrity result must match.
contract.object_boundary: Every database-referenced snapshot or governed artifact is enumerated exactly once, copied as bytes to a distinct declared recovery domain, read back and rehashed; manifest-only backups fail.
contract.restore_boundary: Restore targets must be fresh/empty and distinct from source/recovery inputs. Old targets remain read-only; no overwrite, downgrade, delete or reset is recovery.
contract.authority_boundary: Local separate roots and disposable databases prove mechanics only. The user's at-most-one-cycle loss direction remains a target until named owner, accepted RTO/retention/provider and repeated real drills exist.
